body.statement:
Assume the fixed Hölder radii have positive interior slack, so \(c_\circ>0\), and let the nonzero Fourier weights of the fixed periodic kernel, ordered decreasingly, satisfy \(c_kj^{-2r}\le a_{(j)}\le C_kj^{-2r}\), with \(a_0>0\). For every sufficiently small dyadic \(h\), every full-data extension \(P_\omega,Q_\omega\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}fuzzy\mbox{-}mixtures}\) satisfies consistency and exchangeability and has \(\eta\le e_\omega\le1-\eta\). Quantitatively, \(\|e_\omega-1/2\|_{\mathcal H^{ eta_e}}\le C_ga_hh^{- eta_e}/2=C_gc_\circ/2\). Under \(P_\omega\), \(
u_{0,\omega}=
u_{1,\omega}=
u_\star+v_\omega b_Y/2\) and \(\|
u_{a,\omega}-
u_\star\|_{\mathcal H^{ eta_m}(\mathcal H_Y)}\le C_gb_hh^{- eta_m}\|b_Y\|_{\mathcal H_Y}/2\). Under \(Q_\omega\), \[
u_{1,\omega}=
u_\star- rac{v_\omega(1-u_\omega)}{2(1+u_\omega)}b_Y,\qquad 
u_{0,\omega}=
u_\star- rac{v_\omega(1+u_\omega)}{2(1-u_\omega)}b_Y,\] and \(\max_a\|
u_{a,\omega}-
u_\star\|_{\mathcal H^{ eta_m}(\mathcal H_Y)}\le C_{\mathrm{arm}}b_hh^{- eta_m}\|b_Y\|_{\mathcal H_Y}=C_{\mathrm{arm}}c_\circ\|b_Y\|_{\mathcal H_Y}\). Hence the declared overlap and Hölder conditions hold by the definition of \(c_\circ\), rather than by assuming membership of the fuzzy family. There are constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{IF}}<C_{\mathrm{IF}}<\infty\), depending only on the displayed fixed bounds, such that for every component law \[c_{\mathrm{IF}}C_{k,b}(P_X)\preceq\Sigma_{P_\omega},\Sigma_{Q_\omega}\preceq C_{\mathrm{IF}}C_{k,b}(P_X).\] Consequently the density band and the Fourier profile imply \(c_{\mathrm{IF}}c_Xc_k\|b_Y\|_{\mathcal H_Y}^2j^{-2r}\le\mu_j(P_\omega),\mu_j(Q_\omega)\le C_{\mathrm{IF}}C_XC_k\|b_Y\|_{\mathcal H_Y}^2j^{-2r}\); whenever the fixed \(c_\Sigma,C_\Sigma\) bracket these derived constants, all components satisfy the declared covariance profile. For \(0<s\le1/2\), the same lower operator bound and the representation \(\Psi(Q_\omega)=E[K_X\otimes U_{Q_\omega}(X)]\) give \[\sum_{j\ge1}\mu_j(Q_\omega)^{-2s}|\langle\Psi(Q_\omega),v_j(Q_\omega)angle_{\mathcal H}|^2=\|\Sigma_{Q_\omega}^{-s}\Psi(Q_\omega)\|_{\mathcal H}^2\le C_s\|U_{Q_\omega}\|_{L^2(P_X;\mathcal H_Y)}^2\le C_s'a_h^2b_h^2,\] which is at most \(R^2\) for small \(h\). Finally, writing \(\overline P_h^{(n)}=2^{-K_h}\sum_\omega P_\omega^{\otimes n}\) and \(\overline Q_h^{(n)}=2^{-K_h}\sum_\omega Q_\omega^{\otimes n}\), \[\chi^2(\overline Q_h^{(n)},\overline P_h^{(n)})\le\exp\{C n(n-1)a_h^2b_h^2\sum_{j=1}^{K_h}p_{h,j}^2\}-1.\] Under uniform design, \(\sum_jp_{h,j}^2=h^d\); choosing \(h=c_hn^{-2/(2t+d)}\) with a sufficiently small fixed \(c_h>0\) makes the mixture affinity bounded away from zero while \(\|\Psi(Q_\omega)\|_{\mathcal H}\ge c h^t\).
body.justification: This isolates every model-membership and affinity inequality needed to turn the corrected cell algebra into a legal all-tests lower bound.
body.gap: Neither scalar CATE lower bounds nor direct kernel tests verify Hilbert arm smoothness, influence-covariance stability, and covariance-dependent source membership for the same exact-null causal mixture.
body.consumer: The lemma makes the nuisance lower theorem reusable and gives the arbitrary-density question a concrete construction whose remaining difficulty is the occupancy match, not basic legality.
